cells.tense: Strength is moving outward from you now, by measure, and it lands where it is needed.
cells.act: choose which star to steer by and steer
cells.ask: Pick the season you want next and what it's for, then take a single step toward it that a friend would notice.
cells.core:
You can hand strength to someone and still have enough left for your own day. What you pass along tends to land where it's needed, and people settle near you without knowing why. That's a real skill, and it isn't the same as being endlessly available.

Something is still unspent, though. You've kept your strength moving without deciding what the whole of it is for. Name the direction you actually want, not the one that keeps things smooth, and take one step in it this week. Not a plan. One step, where a friend would notice it happen. Strength that goes somewhere carries further than strength scattered in every direction at once.
cells.sheetLine: You can give and still have enough.
cells.verb: to share strength outward, in measure, with the people near you
cells.place: in the open field before anything has been chosen

cells.tense: You will have handed your strength out past what you had, and you will still be looking for the next one who needs it.
cells.act: keep your own count of what is owed, and pay it
cells.ask: Set who you're helping and what each cost beside what comes back to you, and see whether the two sides line up.
cells.core:
You're spending ahead. Someone needs something and your hand is already open — money, hours, the strength to fix it — before you've checked whether it was yours to carry. From the outside this still looks like generosity. From the inside it's getting hard to tell where helping ends and bracing begins. When you've given past your own supply, the ones close to you start needing you to be fine, and nobody says so.

Giving less isn't the answer. Being honest about the ledger is. List who you're carrying and what it costs, beside what they carry for you. Two columns, no rounding in your own favour. Keep the page private. You'll see the shape of it in about a minute — where there's surplus, and where you've been paying quietly and calling it love.

cells.tense: You were strong enough to carry things to people once, and the carrying stopped.
cells.act: drop the wrong approach and keep the commitment
cells.ask: Think of somebody you still mean to stand by, and change how you reach them — a different contact, or a smaller one — even if the old way is what you know.
cells.core:
You are not hard or stingy. Some form of giving got set down at a point you may not remember choosing, and being set down became the norm. The people who used to get your help have quietly stopped asking. A door you meant to walk back through is still behind you, and you haven't noticed that it's behind you.

You don't have to get big again. Pick somebody you still mean to stand by, and change the method — a shorter visit, a different kind of help, one thing instead of everything. The commitment stays; the way you meet it doesn't have to look like it used to. Small works here. What got interrupted wasn't your strength. It was the form you were doing it in.

cells.tense: You are already steering by a direction you chose, and it has not been named as yours.
cells.act: turn toward the one direction and stop surveying
cells.ask: Look at where your effort went this week, find the heading it kept, and say that heading was your choice.
cells.core:
Something in your life has been turning toward a chosen direction and gathering weight, and it isn't filed under your name. You may be calling it circumstances, or how the month went, or what someone needed. It's been a heading the whole time. Support moves by measure, and you've been metering — choosing what gets your strength and what doesn't — while the deciding stayed off the record.

Stop surveying. More than one direction was open, and the one you keep returning to is the one. Say it plainly, in a sentence, as something you picked. That may feel like overclaiming. It isn't. The steering has been yours throughout, and the only thing missing is your own word on it — one sentence, where you can see it.
cells.sheetLine: You've been heading somewhere by choice. Put your name on it.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that what is unspent still moves outward toward people; the record says support is underway, not that it reaches anyone here, so a reader could reasonably say the giving is only happening inside them.
